activity_context.topic_title: The Parametric Equations of a Plane

feedback.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $D(6,2,1)$ and is parallel to the lines $r=⟨\frac{1}{2},1,9⟩+s⟨4,-1,5⟩$ and $r=⟨\sqrt{3},10,-1⟩+t⟨0,2,3⟩.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The direction vectors of the lines are ${v}_{1}=⟨4,-1,5⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨0,2,3⟩$, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point $D(6,2,1)$ lies on the plane and its position vector is $d=⟨6,2,1⟩.$  

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =d+s{v}_{1}+t{v}_{2} \\ r & =⟨6,2,1⟩+s⟨4,-1,5⟩+t⟨0,2,3⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
